Report Details

Violation Code: 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
Violation ID: 918349
Permit API: 015-20705
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/24/2021
Comments: I met Chris Lee (Chesapeake) at the excavated area at the beginning of the access road who explained the following: This morning they finished excavating soil contaminated by a ~70 gallon diesel fuel release from a truck's tank. The excavated material is in containment further up the access road (photo). They collected soil samples and sent them to a lab today also. Chesapeake will go through Act 2 for cleanup standards. I used a MiniRAE 3000 Photoionization Detector (PID) with a 10.6 eV lamp to get a 6.3 ppm reading under the plastic liner in the excavated area, indicating there is some residual volatile substance emitting from the soil. Violations for the diesel release are cited to 015-20705 well permit. Halliburton is hydraulically fracturing the 3 Marcellus wells at this site. I did not see any pooled liquid on site. Air temp 63F JLP

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8251181
Permit API: 051-24270
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/03/2025
Comments: On October 3 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3265061 of the OGM 1 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of inspection, an Act 9 sign was installed at the access road. The access road appeared stable with no observed accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns. The well appeared equipped for production. No fluid leaks are observed around the well head and associated equipment. A well tag was present with all required information. The GPU appeared to be in sound condition with no fluid leaks or discharges observed.In the Department's previous inspection on 5/15/2025 (IR 3979004), elevated conductivity readings were obtained in an area of a suspected release near the production tank. Upon inspection of this area during today's inspection, a roll of dumpster from McCutcheon Enterprises was on site and appeared to be full. There appeared to be fresh gravel in the location of previously elevated conductivity readings/suspected release area.The Department obtained conductivity readings in similar locations of the previously elevated readings and obtained readings of 0.05mS, 0.09mS, and 0.07mS. These readings were comparable/lower than the background conductivity reading of 0.14mS.The Department received a response from the operator on 5/29/2025 stating: "We will inspect site and check soil for possible need of removal". The Department has not received any further communication regarding remediation of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for/or how remediation of the release was conducted. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection violations under IR 3265061 will remain outstanding for the release pending receipt and review of the requested information.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2014-07-23 to Cabot Oil &Amp; Gas Corp in Gibson Twp, Susquehanna county. 402CSL - Failure to adopt pollution prevention measures required or prescribed by DEP by handling materials that create a danger of pollution.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Cabot Oil &Amp; Gas Corp
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2014-07-23
Violation Code 402CSL - Failure to adopt pollution prevention measures required or prescribed by DEP by handling materials that create a danger of pollution.
Violation ID 701814
Permit API 115-21019
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Gibson Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2014-07-23
Comments Steve Watson of Cabot contacted the PADEP Northeast Regional Office Emergency Response Team at 18:12 on 7/22/14 to a report a spill of (42) gallons of glycol. Mr. Watson indicated during the phone call, that due to a compromised check valve approximately (42) gallons of glycol spilled onto a concrete pad and approximately (5) gallons spilled onto dirt. Mr. Watson stated that the spill occurred due to a dump line washing out on the L Aldrich 1H Gas Production Unit. Due to excessive pressure or sand, the wash out of the dump line created a hole in the glycol bath. Glycol was released out of the hole inside the GPU eventually escaping the unit and impacting the concrete containment for the L1H GPU and 2H GPU and the ground surface of the well pad next to the units. Staining and pools of glycol were observed inside and outside of the units and in an excavation (1) to (1.5) feet below the pad surface next to the concrete containment of the 1H GPU. The spill is now estimated to be between (3-5) barrels, with 2-4) barrels impacting pad surface, Potential for pollutional substances to enter the waters of the commonwealth.

Comments: On August 10 2022 a routine inspection of Errett 1 OG Well was conducted. Accompanying in today's inspection was Adam Clark (ET) and Samantha Foulk (WQSS). The findings were as follows:Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring (see photo 2). Well tag and posting with required information was present on well head(see photo 3). There appears to be a crack in the brine tank (see photo 5) that is causing leakage of fluid on the ground (see photo 6). The leak at the base of the brine tank appears to be active as the base of the brine tank was wet. A conductivity reading was taken at the base of the crack and a background reading was also taken. Reading at the base of the crack 14.35 mS and background was 0.19 mS. Dave Lindahl from Mountain V Oil and Gas, Inc. was contacted and made aware of the situation. The Department request additional information:1. What was released?2. When the release occurred?3. How long was the release occurring?4. Why the release occurred?5. The quantity of the release and how the quantity was determined?The Department also requests disposal records/manifests for the removal of all impacted materials once available. The Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring.Based on today's observations violations will be issued for failure to properly collect and dispose of production fluids under (78.54, 78.57a, 91.34a and SMWA301).

Comments: 08/09/2023This administrative inspection is being conducted for the Ironman Well Site following violations issued on 07/18/2023 (IR: 3589336, Enf: 418538).Violations of 78a57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.33(A), 91.34(A), 78a54, and SWMA 301 were issued on 07/18/2023, following an incident inspection conducted in response to a spill report recieved by the Department on 07/17/2023. On 08/02/2023, the Department recieved the 15 Day Report. The following is required to be included within the 15 day report, however deficiencies were noted within, specifically A, D, E, and G: 78a.66. Reporting and remediating spills and releases. (c)(2)(i) Within 15 business days of the spill or release, the operator or other responsible party shall provide an initial written report that includes, to the extent that the information is available, the following:(A) The regulated substance involved.(B) The location where the spill or release occurred.(C) The environmental media affected.(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities.(F) Interim remedial actions planned, initiated or completed.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible partyintends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedulefor site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated timeframes within which it expects to take those actions.The following deficiencies were noted within the 15 Day Report submitted on 08/02/2023:(A) The regulated substance involved: EQT's report mentions leak from dump line, but does not specifically mention the regulated substance.(C) EQT's report did not mention an assessment of potential impact to Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible party intends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedule for site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated time frames within which it expects to take those actions: EQT mentions entering Act 2, but provides no timeline. EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. Violations issued on 07/18/2023 remain outstanding.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8242766
Permit API: 117-22232
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Lawrence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/30/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at JKLM Energy's TSF 12 Well Site located in Lawrence Township, Tioga County on 7/30/2025 at 1110 hours. The weather was 85 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by JKLM. JKLM reported that on 7/30/2025 at ~0801 hours, a pressure regulating "Kimray" valve on a gas production unit's dump line washed out on the bottom. The washout resulted in a spray/mist of produced fluids to reach the pad surface impacting the gravel material. An estimated 25 to 35 gallons of produced fluids was released to the pad surface. An area ~16ft by 13ft by ~2 inches deep was delineated as impacted. JKLM reported that the production unit dumps ~three quarters of a barrel of produced fluids through the line at intervals and only one dump interval was able to escape the line.During my inspection, the valve was in the process of being replaced. A hydrovac truck was dispatched and was en route to the site for remediation to begin. Due to the release being under and around piping infrastructure, the hydrovac will be utilized to recover impacted material rather than using excavation equipment. The impacted area can be seen in photo #2. I field measured the pad material within the impacted area and received readings for electrical conductivity ranging from 2.7 to >4.0mS/cm. Once collected, the impacted material will be stored in a residual waste container for later disposal. A representative with JKLM will be using a soil probe to guide the remediation efforts. The hydrovac truck arrived onsite prior to my departure. JKLM later provided me with an update and photos of the area after remediation was completed (see photos #3 and 4). After removing material, it was noted that excavation efforts went 7-8 inches deep in some spots where the fluids were stopped by a soil cement layer. The area was cleaned up to visible.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the following violations are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-22232:CSL 402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a), and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1205 hours.

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8170406
Permit API: 083-53759
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well. This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. There are no apparent surface issues on the location location or the spur road leading to it.A tank battery located along FR 370 approximately 250 feet northwest of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks (11883 and 11884) within an earthen containment. There is evidence of repeated discharges of production water inside of the containment from each tank. Soil specific conductance (SPC) readings upwards of 15,000 uS/cm were detected at/downslope of the drains located on the back side of each tank. Elevated SPC is prevalent across the ground inside of the containment downslope of the tanks. Accumulated fluid pooled along the western wall of the containment has an SPC over 20,000 uS/cm. There was no active discharge at time of inspection.The fluids released inside of the containment have seeped through the northern corner of the earthen containment wall (or there is a buried drain) at 41.99216N / 78.76119 W. There is an approximate 25' x 3' area of stained soil with elevated SPC (upwards of 818 uS/cm vs 40 uS/cm of nearby uncontaminated soil) present outside of the containment's northern corner. The end of the apparent contaminated soil is located approximately 75 feet from Yeager Brook.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery containment to contain fluid inside of it will also nee to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Permit API: 053-28071
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/25/2024
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. The GPS coordinate on file for this well was verified as part of this inspection. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty stuffing box on this well. The discharged crude oil migrated onto the well site, then traveled linearly approximately 450 feet downslope of the well on the access road. The crude oil remained contained on the road surface and ultimately accumulated in a puddle of standing water at the bottom of the hill (see Photo 2). It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.A representative from Bull Run Resources, JR McLaughlin, was contacted in response to the event. He arrived to the site immediately to address the noted concerns. The leaking stuffing box was repaired and diapers were used to absorb the crude oil from the road surface and around the well head. Given there is no ongoing discharge and a bulk of the released product has been remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected.A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Violation ID: 8189738
Permit API: 129-26861
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: On June 4th, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/4/24 at 12:04 PM (CTS 381210). Present at today's inspection is William Warfel of Diversified Energy.At the time of this inspection, William stated that at 10:30 AM on 6/4/24 while onsite at the Davenport well, they had noticed some staining on the gravel underneath the production tank valve and a large patch of dead vegetation downslope of the well site. After using measuring devices to gauge the fluid level in the production tank, it was determined that approximately 18-20 barrels had released from the production tank. William stated that prior to the Department arriving onsite, a water truck had already come and emptied the remainder of the production tank. The production tank once empty, was then moved adjacent to where it once sat so that removal of contaminated material could begin. William showed the Department a small area on the valve pipe of the production tank where they believe the leak came from. The Department observed a dried white chalky substance on this area of the valve pipe presumed to be dried brine water. William hypothesizes that the brine water travel down the shale bank adjacent to where the production tank used to sit and pooled in the once grassy lot downslope of the well site.Upon observation of the area downslope of the production tank, the Department noticed an approximately 15ft by 8ft area of dead vegetation and mud with sheeny/iridescent puddles throughout. The Department then took a soil conductivity reading upslope of the production tank in some vegetation adjacent to the well site as a background (0.1337 mS), another in the stained gravel underneath where the production tank valve hole was (1.35 mS), and then on the shale hill leading down to the now dead vegetation adjacent to well site (1.454 mS). Then the Department began taking soil conductivity readings at the bottom of this hill to gauge how wide of an area the spill impacted. A soil conductivity reading was taken in a sheeny/iridescent puddle observed in some mud that was surrounded by dead vegetation (Over range), it was evident that all areas lacking vegetation and that were visibly wet and iridescent were impacted, so the Department went to the edge of this area to determine if any vegetated areas were impacted as well. The dead vegetation looks to be a pathway of where the release may have traveled and it leads right up to a small wooded area. Soil conductivty readings were taken at the edge of the dead vegetation where it meets the wooded area (7.63mS), another taken adjacent to the previous reading in a spot that is also where the dead vegetation meets the woods (5.51 mS), in the wooden area about 1 foot from the dead vegetation (4.90 mS) and even further in the wooded area, about 3 feet in from the dead vegetation (0.1747 mS). A reading was also taken in the grass to the left of the dead vegetation (0.280 mS) to see if that grassy area was impacted as well. These soil conductivity readings subjugate that the impacted area goes beyond where you can visibly see puddles and dead vegetation. While onsite the Department let William know that areas outside of the dead vegetation area are elevated and recommended that when removing contaminated material they give themselves a buffer area larger than 3 feet in each direction. William stated that Spartan Specialty Services would be onsite soon to place impacted soil and gravel into dumpsters and that details will be provided in the Act 2 summary report. William stated that silt fences will also be installed to ensure there are not any erosion and sedimentation issues during the removal process.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for this 18-20 barrel release of brine fluid onto the gravel well site and the adjacent grass lot and wooded area.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 890375
Permit API: 047-23569
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 07/31/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill that was found the morning of 7/31/2020. Per the operator, a leak of brine occurred from a poly tank or the line leading from the separator to the tank and leaked into containment. It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. Vegetation within the containment is distressed or dead, indicating brine discharge. Down slope from the containment, vegetation has been killed in a band consistent with discharge from or around the freshwater drain. Conductivity measured ~11 mS near the drain and diminished down slope, with the final reading over 1 mS noted approximately 100 feet from the tank, in a scour location that was likely from a stormwater event. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KRIEBEL ACQUISITION CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/04/2023
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 980669
Permit API: 129-27065
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/04/2023
Comments: On January 4, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well site in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and DEP OGI Patrick Hiles. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3453961, during which remediation efforts were made by the operator in response to IR 3446144, where impacted soil was discovered by the Department.The following was observed:The well site excavation has been backfilled since IR 3453961 (see photos 2 and 5). The site appeared to be stabile with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or sedimentation, and was mulched and seeded. The excavation stockpile remains placed atop a sheet of black plastic (see photo 1). However, it was uncovered unlike the operator and contractor reported. The well head was equipped with a well tag (see photo 3). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of leaks or discharge (see photo 4). Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation stockpile to ensure that contamination has not leached into the ground. Elevated conductivity was found immediately downslope of the stockpile, on its west side (see photos 6, 7, and 9). Additional readings were taken approximately 4 feet further downslope from this point, and around the rest of the stockpile (see photos 8, 10, 11, and 12). No additional elevated readings were gathered. Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been excavated from the area of release. However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Because this contamination appears to be localized close to the stockpile, the Department recommends immediate remediation and proper storage to prevent the contamination from spreading. Also, the Department once again requests an approximate quantity released from the brine tank, and the waste manifest when available.

Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCOOL JOHN E
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8278643
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: On 3/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 32 degrees and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. On 3/6/2023 Chesapeake personnel identified a water puddle on the unprotected pad surface with elevated conductance on the southwest corner of the pad in the location where chemical ASTs and a freshwater AST were stationed during recent frac operations. No release was reported in this area during the frac or drilling operations. It is expected that an unknown quantity of produced water or brine may have been released during fracking operations. They began excavating the area and had removed 20 truckloads when they contacted the department on 3/7/2023 to report the release. They continued removing material and were still excavating during this inspection. The excavated material was being hauled to the Chesapeake Stoorza well site for temporary storage prior to disposal.I met Creston Envirionmental's Andrew Steffe, who was field testing water and soil from and around the excavation. Andrew reported that he had gotten readings as high as 50 mS conductance from a water puddle that was in the area being excavated. Readings from the soils ranged from 0.1 mS conductance to 6.0 mS conductance. We measured the current extent of the excavation at 162' x 50'. It was approximately 3' deep. A water puddle in the bottom of west end of the excavated area field tested at 15.95 mS conductance. I field tested water in two test pits that were near the north side of the excavated area; water in the east pit was 6.13 mS conductance and the west pit was >20.0 mS conductance. The upper limit of the Oakton PCTS-50 is 20.0 mS conductance. Andrew said that the excavation would continue until he got readings that were under 1.0 mS conductance.I field tested water on the northeast corner of the pad with results at 1.3 mS, 0.5 mS, and 0.5 mS. Drilling mats were being pressure washed on the northwest corner of the pad, the washing being conducted over secondary containment. Water on the east side of the drilling mat wash station field tested at 1.4 mS conductance and on the west side field tested at 0.6 mS conductance. Water in the wash station secondary containment field tested at 1.8 mS conductance.There are five wells on site. Crews were in the process of putting the five wells into production. API/well permit numbers are posted at the entrance to the site. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank were not connected to the wellheads yet.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was witnessed in some areas. PCSM is addressed on site by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place below the infiltration areasThis spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)I left the site at 1145 hrs.

Comments: On September 19, 2024, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View's George A Willlaims 4 well located in South Huntington Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3726379 where violations were issued for a spill from the production tank. A Notice of Violation response was received by the Department on May 16, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road which is off of a residential home's driveway appears stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the well site is located in a field adjacent to the residence home. The production tank that was leaking during IR 3726379 appears to be removed from the well site and the area where it sat appears to be the only area of the well site that is lacking 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. A well tag is fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the well head. Production equipment on site appears to be heavily rusted, the Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the production equipment to ensure corrosion does not worsen and compromise the structural integrity.A background soil conductivity reading was taken in some vegetation up slope of the well site (0.1781 mS) and then several soil conductivity readings were taken in the area where the production tank once sat (0.562 mS, 0.718 mS, 0.1278 mS, 0.229 mS, 0.582 mS, 0.539 mS, 0.1788 mS, 0.619 mS, and 0.1467 mS). Based on today's inspection, violations issue during IR 3726379 shall remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: On August 12 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator to the Department on 8/12/2022 for the Huffys Family Unit 16H OG Well. The Department was accompanied by Derek Zofchak(Range Resources) and Chase Kolence(Range Resources). The findings were as follows:Per Mr. Zofchak, produced water was released due to a corrisive elbow on production equipment(see photo 9). It was estimated that approximately 10 gallons of produced water was released onto the ground next to the 16H GPU. The 16H GPU failed to be in secondary containment. The Department request that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct follow up inspection to verify all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's observations violations will be issued under (78a54, 78a57a, 91.34a and SWMA 301).

Comments: Bull Run Resources contacted WQSS Brian Ayers to inform him of a release that occurred overnight on April 16, 2025 their Peterson P9 well, located in Pleasant Twp Warren County. The emergency low pressure switch on the well head also did not function as designed. Production fluid was released from the well head and traveled downslope following a series of road ditches and culvert crossings. The release does not appear to have progressed past a power line located just north of the well. Several underflow dams have been constructed in the ditch lines and are working effectively at this time. Absorbent pads are being used at the siphon dams to collect any production fluid accumulating behind them. The quantity of the release is estimated between one half to one barrel. Bull Run was having roll off dumpsters delivered while I was onsite. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility.Upon completion of the remediation, confirmatory samples are expected to be collected and their results provided to the Department. Documentation verifying the disposal of the impacted soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8226934
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/25/2025
Comments: On March 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3484420, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2, 4, and 5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head closest to the well head was observed on the ground. The Department recommends that this top hatch is replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater (see photo 6).The well postings on-site include contact information for Murphy Production, Inc. The well tag is affixed to the well head with Murphy Production Inc listed on the tag along with the permit number and well name (see photo 8, 11, and 13).No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 10). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 9). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site.The access road is stabilized with gravel. The well is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 3 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued under IR 3484420 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/27/2022 to PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in North Shenango Twp, Crawford county. 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/27/2022
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 970189
Permit API: 039-25765
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: North Shenango Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2022
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint ID #366445 that is dated 8/22/2022.The complainant indicated to the Department that they had concerns regarding the installation of a stormwater discharge pipe at the site. It was stated that the stormwater basin recently overtopped and flooded the adjacent township roadway. Based upon the information from the complainant the operator installed a new discharge pipe that outlets to the roadside ditch of the township road. The ditch flows into UNT to Bennett Run (WWF).Based upon my investigation and site inspection the Department finds the following: -It appears that the sediment basins did overflow and discharge stormwater into the woods and out onto the township road.Recent activity indicates:-The two sediment basins have been cleaned out of sediment.-An earth berm along the wood line has been established between the two basins.-A graded channel/swale has been created between the basins. The southern basin flows through the swale to the northern basin.-There are several rock filters within the swale/channel.-It appears that a 4" PVC pipe has been installed from the northern basin and day lights to the roadside ditch of the township road. (Currently flowing water)The recent activity at the site regarding the post construction stormwater management of the site was not approved by the Department. The activity was not part of the original permit and therefore the operator is in violation.The site has mot been restored per state requirements for restoration and therefore is still in violation for site restoration.The well is properly labeled and there is a Site ID posting at the entrance of the site. The well appears to be shut-in and not plumbed to produce. There is a vertical separator and a 210bbl steel tank onsite in separate lined containment structures. The containment should be monitored for stormwater removal to allow for appropriate capacity of the containment. There are also several other pieces of equipment onsite including: a natural gas-powered electric generator skid and several steel structures for bitcoin computer generation. A contractor onsite during the inspection indicated that the equipment was being dismantled and removed from the site.The operator has reported "no" production for the well from January 2022 through July 2022. Seven consecutive months reported with no production. The Department requests information regarding the intentions of the operator to produce the well within the the next 3 months. A well is required to produce within a 12 month period to maintain "Active" status. Otherwise, the well is considered to be abandoned. Outstanding / New violations are cited.
